tldr_label: TL;DR: Abu Dhabi talks end without a breakthrough, the House shelves Hegseth impeachment, and hot inflation data halts the rally

tldr_bullets.label: Ukraine
tldr_bullets.body: Two days of US-mediated talks in Abu Dhabi closed with a short session and no announced breakthrough. Territory and security guarantees remain unresolved. [[TAG:warning:no breakthrough]]

tldr_bullets.label: Washington
tldr_bullets.body: The House voted 211-204 to send Massie's articles against Hegseth to committee, effectively ending the effort in this Congress. The Senate races in Alaska and Mississippi remain uncalled. [[TAG:info:shelved for now]]

tldr_bullets.label: Inflation
tldr_bullets.body: October CPI rose 0.4% and core CPI 0.3%, both above forecasts. Stocks fell and bets on a Fed hike rose. [[TAG:danger:hot print]]

tldr_bullets.label: Iran
tldr_bullets.body: Trump said the war is militarily 'effectively over.' Tehran denied that talks are planned and said no enriched uranium will leave the country. [[TAG:warning:mixed signals]]

tldr_bullets.label: Israel
tldr_bullets.body: Eisenkot's party cancelled a negotiating session with Likud after a Netanyahu speech it called divisive. [[TAG:warning:talks stall]]

sections.title: Ukraine: Abu Dhabi Ends, Europe Splits
sections.summary: Short final session yields no announced breakthrough; four EU states defy Merz on aid

paragraphs.heading: Second Day
paragraphs.body: TASS reported that the final session in Abu Dhabi lasted just under two hours, with Vladimir Medinsky leading Russia's delegation and Rustem Umerov leading Ukraine's. RFE/RL said a brief meeting wrapped up the two days after a night of air attacks by both sides. Euronews said no breakthrough was announced, and that territory and security guarantees remained the focus. A Yahoo News report said more talks are expected next week. [[TAG:warning:no breakthrough]]

paragraphs.heading: Readouts Diverge
paragraphs.body: France 24 reported that Zelensky welcomed Europe's inclusion in the process. According to the coverage reviewed, a Russian source said the Kremlin had no contact with European representatives in Abu Dhabi, while Kyiv said its negotiators would meet European envoys separately. MarketScreener carried a report that Ukraine's foreign minister accused Putin of attacking 'cynically' during the talks. [[TAG:info:Europe's role contested]]

paragraphs.heading: Budget Fight
paragraphs.body: Euronews reported that Slovakia, the Czech Republic, Hungary and Bulgaria rejected Chancellor Merz's demand to make German approval of the 2028-2034 EU budget conditional on all member states closing Ukraine's roughly 70 billion euro funding gap. Slovak Prime Minister Robert Fico called it 'blackmail' and threatened a veto. Czech leader Andrej Babis argued the draft budget already earmarks 100 billion euros for Ukraine. The budget requires unanimity. [[TAG:danger:veto threat]]

sections.title: Iran: 'Effectively Over'?
sections.summary: Trump declares the war militarily over after Qatar meeting; Tehran denies talks are planned

paragraphs.heading: Trump's Claim
paragraphs.body: AP, via WRTV and AOL, reported that after meeting Qatar's prime minister, Trump said he believes the war with Iran is militarily 'effectively over.' Iran International reported that he called new strikes 'quite unlikely' but said the US remains ready to strike. The naval blockade remains in place, according to the reports. [[TAG:info:blockade stays]]

paragraphs.heading: Tehran's Denial
paragraphs.body: Euronews reported that Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi denied that any meeting with the US was planned. Iran says it will not negotiate until Washington takes concrete steps on its seven conditions. Deccan Herald and Middle East Eye reported that Supreme National Security Council secretary Mohsen Rezaei said Iran will not allow enriched nuclear material to leave the country. Washington has reportedly sought the transfer of Iran's stockpile. [[TAG:danger:uranium red line]]

sections.title: Washington
sections.summary: House refers Hegseth articles to committee 211-204; Alaska and Mississippi still counting

paragraphs.heading: Impeachment Shelved
paragraphs.body: NPR and NBC News reported that the House voted 211-204 on Tuesday to send Rep. Thomas Massie's resolution against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth to committee, effectively ending the effort. Massie was the only Republican to break with his party. The eight articles focused on the Iran war and military operations in Yemen, Venezuela and the Caribbean. Time reported that Democrats could revive the effort when they take control of the House in January. Trump called the outcome an 'EXONERATION.' [[TAG:info:could return in 2027]]

paragraphs.heading: Senate Count
paragraphs.body: CNBC reported that Democrat Scott Colom has extended a narrow lead over Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith in Mississippi, with about 30,000 votes outstanding. KCRA reported that Mary Peltola leads Sen. Dan Sullivan by about 2,500 votes in Alaska, a race that could go to ranked-choice tabulation and where late mail ballots can still arrive. [[TAG:warning:two races open]]

sections.title: Markets: Hot Inflation
sections.summary: October CPI tops forecasts and Wall Street slips; Korean chip stocks lead an Asian rebound

paragraphs.heading: CPI Surprise
paragraphs.body: CNBC and Morningstar reported that the consumer price index rose 0.4% in October and core prices rose 0.3%, both above expectations. Outlets differ on the consensus, citing a headline forecast of 0.2% or 0.3%. The BLS published no annual rate because last year's government shutdown disrupted data collection. Coverage reported that Dallas Fed President Lorie Logan, speaking after the report, sees a need for two more quarter-point rate increases. [[TAG:danger:hike bets rise]]

paragraphs.heading: Wall Street
paragraphs.body: The Washington Post and the Motley Fool reported that the Dow fell about 0.3%, the S&P 500 0.38% and the Nasdaq 0.74% on Tuesday, ending a two-day rally. Treasury yields jumped. Coverage said Nvidia was a major drag, falling about 5% as scrutiny of CEO Jensen Huang continued. [[TAG:warning:rally stalls]]

paragraphs.heading: Asia and Oil
paragraphs.body: investingLive reported that Japan's Nikkei rose for a third day on Wednesday and South Korea's Kosdaq jumped about 5% at midday as AI stocks rebounded. Investing.com said falling oil prices also lifted sentiment. Midday and closing figures for the Kospi vary across outlets. [[TAG:success:chip rebound]]

sections.title: Israel: Talks Hit a Snag
sections.summary: Eisenkot cancels a Likud session after Netanyahu's Knesset speech; Likud says it remains open

paragraphs.heading: Session Cancelled
paragraphs.body: The Times of Israel and Israel Hayom reported that Eisenkot's Yashar party cancelled a scheduled negotiating session with Likud after Netanyahu's speech at the Knesset swearing-in, which the party said showed he 'does not want unity.' The Jerusalem Post said the party set conditions for Likud joining, including cutting ties with partners it calls extremist and serving in a government led by Eisenkot. Likud said it remains open to talks but criticized Eisenkot's contacts with Arab parties. [[TAG:warning:unity talks stall]]

paragraphs.heading: Clock Ticking
paragraphs.body: Haaretz reported that Avigdor Liberman's courtship of the Haredi parties, in pursuit of a 61-seat coalition without Arab-party support, is slowing Eisenkot's effort and risks using up the mandate period. The Times of Israel reported that Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich urged the Haredi parties to reject talks with Eisenkot's bloc, and that UTJ is moving to cement draft exemptions. [[TAG:info:61 needed]]

sections.title: Taiwan and APEC
sections.summary: Taipei names Acer founder Stan Shih as APEC envoy and asks Beijing for written guarantees

paragraphs.heading: Envoy Named
paragraphs.body: Reuters, via Yahoo News and The Standard, reported that President Lai Ching-te appointed Acer founder Stan Shih, 81, as Taiwan's envoy to the APEC leaders' meeting in Shenzhen on November 18 and 19. Taipei asked China, as host, to provide a written guarantee that its delegation can take part in all meetings on equal terms and in safety. China's Taiwan Affairs Office said it handles Taiwan's participation under the one-China principle. Shih also represented Taiwan at APEC in 2007. [[TAG:info:summit next week]]

sections.title: Around the World
sections.summary: COP31 leaders gather without the US; Pope ends Argentina tour; Kenya discharges last Ebola patient

paragraphs.heading: COP31 Summit
paragraphs.body: Report.az said UN Secretary-General Guterres and about 102 leaders were expected at the COP31 leaders' summit opening in Antalya on Wednesday. BusinessWorld, citing Reuters, said the United States is skipping the talks for a second year and that negotiators are seeking a plan to raise electricity's share of global energy use. Hurriyet Daily News said the Turkish presidency is putting electrification at the center of its implementation push. [[TAG:info:leaders summit]]

paragraphs.heading: Pope Heads Home
paragraphs.body: France 24 and AP, via the Washington Post, reported that Pope Leo XIV ends his Argentina tour on Wednesday with a visit to a prison linked to the military dictatorship and an outdoor Mass at the shrine of Our Lady of Lujan, before flying to Peru, where he served for years as a missionary and bishop. Euronews reported large crowds in Córdoba after a record Mass in Buenos Aires. [[TAG:success:Peru homecoming]]

paragraphs.heading: Ebola
paragraphs.body: The Washington Post and TimesLive reported that Kenya discharged its last Ebola patient on Wednesday and began a 42-day countdown to being declared free of the disease. Kenya has had nine cases and no new infections since October 19. Contagion Live reported that the Bundibugyo-strain outbreak in Congo has passed 10,000 cases. [[TAG:warning:outbreak continues]]
